subject.title: Per-agent tools.selfDeny — allow tool inheritance to subagents while denying direct use

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit delegate-only/self-deny tool policy for requester agents, and which public config shape should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes a public config surface and the security boundary between requester-visible tools and subagent-delegable tools.

options.title: Approve delegate-only config
options.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior for tools denied everywhere.

options.title: Fold into per-spawn policy
options.body: Use child-side `toolsAllow` for narrowing spawned runs and document that parent direct-use prevention still requires separate profiles or prompt guidance until a later design.

options.title: Keep monotonic policy only
options.body: Reject delegate-only inheritance for now and document the security rationale plus the separate-agent workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve delegate-only config
recommendation.body: Add an optional per-agent policy that hides listed tools from the requester model while preserving deny-wins behavior for tools denied everywhere.

likelyOwner.reason: He has adjacent `sessions_spawn` policy history and is the strongest available routing signal for a security-sensitive config/API decision.
